subject: Family & Community Health
question: Which of the following BEST defines Community Diagnosis?
options: A brief survey of diseases in a hospital setting
An in-depth process of finding the health profiles, status
A census conducted by the national statistics office
A clinical assessment of individual patients in a barangay
A rapid screening of communicable diseases only

rationale.text: Community Diagnosis is an in-depth process of finding out the health profiles, health status, and factors affecting the present status of the community — not just listing diseases or individual patients. It gives the full picture of a community's health.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: In conducting community diagnosis, the FIRST step is:
options: Data collection through surveys
Determining the objectives
Conducting an ocular survey
Preparing frequency distributions
Disseminating the findings

rationale.text: Before collecting any data, you must define WHY you are there. Determining the objectives (general and specific) is always Step 1 — like setting your GPS destination before driving.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A group of medical students arrives at Barangay Masaya for their community rotation. Their FIRST activity should be:
options: Administering a health questionnaire to all households
Conducting a focus group discussion with mothers
Making a courtesy call to the barangay captain
Drawing a spot map of the community
Reviewing hospital records from the nearby RHU

rationale.text: Proper community engagement requires a courtesy call to the barangay captain FIRST. This respects local leadership and gains community trust before any data gathering — just as you'd knock before entering someone's home.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Which is classified under Analysis of Population in community diagnosis?
options: Morbidity rates of common diseases
Age and sex structure of the community
Number of health workers available
Proportion of GNP spent on health
Hospital bed-occupancy rate

rationale.text: Analysis of Population covers total population, geographic distribution, age and sex structure, vital indices, and population projections. Age and sex structure tells us WHO lives in the community — shaping what health needs exist.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A medical student computes the number of health workers per 1,000 population in the barangay. This belongs to which component of situational analysis?
options: Analysis of Health Status
Analysis of Socio-economic Factors
Analysis of Health Resources
Analysis of Population
Analysis of Environmental Factors

rationale.text: Manpower-to-population ratios fall under Analysis of Health Resources. This component looks at who provides care and what facilities/equipment are available in the community.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Dr. Santos notices that most families in a barangay rely on farming and have low educational attainment. This is part of which component?
options: Analysis of Health Status
Analysis of Health Resources
Analysis of Socio-economic Factors
Analysis of Population
Analysis of Vital Statistics

rationale.text: Education level and occupation (farming) are classic socio-economic indicators. The Analysis of Socio-economic Factors covers education, employment, income, social support, community safety, and cultural practices — all of which influence health outcomes.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The FOUR STAGES of conducting community diagnosis are:
options: Planning, Implementation, Evaluation, Dissemination
Initiation, Data Collection and Analysis, Diagnosis-Situational Analysis, Dissemination
Survey, Interview, Observation, Recording
Assessment, Planning, Implementation, Monitoring
Identification, Prioritization, Intervention, Evaluation

rationale.text: The four stages: (1) Initiation — getting established in the community; (2) Data Collection and Analysis; (3) Diagnosis/Situational Analysis — interpreting findings; (4) Dissemination — sharing results. Think: START → GATHER → UNDERSTAND → SHARE.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A community assembly is PRIMARILY conducted to:
options: Select barangay health workers
Inform residents of the purpose of your presence and share initial findings
Administer vaccines to the residents
Collect blood samples for laboratory testing
Install water purification systems

rationale.text: The community assembly serves two purposes: (1) inform people WHY you are there, and (2) share initial findings — especially about infectious diseases, their mode of transmission, and signs and symptoms. It is your introduction and public health education moment combined.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: During community assessment, the medical team finds that 40% of households use open-pit latrines and river water for drinking. This information belongs to which component?
options: Analysis of Health Status
Analysis of Socio-economic Factors
Analysis of Health Resources
Analysis of Population
Analysis of Manpower Resources

rationale.text: Sanitation practices and water sources are Environmental Indicators under the Socio-economic component. Poor sanitation directly correlates with infectious disease rates and tells you what environmental risk factors exist.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Physical health indicators in Analysis of Health Status include:
options: Proportion of GNP spent on health
Hospital bed turnover ratio
Maternal mortality rate and infant mortality rate
Proportion of population with health insurance
Number of trained barangay health workers

rationale.text: Health STATUS indicators measure how healthy (or sick) the population actually is — mortality rates (maternal, infant, neonatal) and morbidity data are the actual health outcomes of the community. GNP and hospital beds are resource or policy indicators, not direct health status measures.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The SPOT MAP prepared during ocular survey is used to:
options: Record individual patient clinical findings
Visually display the geographic location of households and health sites
Compile all laboratory results from the RHU
List names of all barangay health workers
Show the floor plan of the health center

rationale.text: A spot map is a visual geographic tool showing WHERE things are located — households, health facilities, disease clusters, water sources, etc. It reveals spatial patterns (e.g., disease cases clustering near a contaminated water source) that raw numbers cannot easily show.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Economic indicators in situational analysis include:
options: Birth rate and death rate
Employment status, income, and family support
Hospital admission rates
Number of nurses per population
Environmental pollution levels

rationale.text: Economic indicators include employment/job status, income level, and family/social support. These determine if people can afford healthcare, nutritious food, and healthy living conditions. Poverty and unemployment are powerful drivers of poor health outcomes.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A community diagnosis is described as a 'PROCESS' because:
options: It is a one-time activity done only during outreach programs
It is a continuing activity with definite periods and ongoing expectations
It requires only government health workers
It only involves quantitative data collection
It replaces the annual census

rationale.text: Community diagnosis is ongoing — not a one-shot deal. As a PROCESS, it has definite periods (phases) with minimum and maximum expectations. Communities change, health problems evolve, so the diagnosis must continue to update over time.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A community diagnosis report states: '1 rural health unit, 3 barangay health stations, and a ratio of 1 nurse per 2,000 population.' This data belongs to which component?
options: Analysis of Health Status
Analysis of Population
Analysis of Socio-economic Factors
Analysis of Health Resources
Analysis of Environmental Indicators

rationale.text: Number and type of health facilities (RHU, BHS) and nurse-to-population ratios are HEALTH RESOURCE indicators — specifically manpower and material resources. These tell you if the community has enough healthcare infrastructure to meet its needs.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Which of the following data collection methods provides FIRST-HAND information directly from community members?
options: Records review
Surveys
Observations
Interviews
Review of census data

rationale.text: Interviews provide first-hand information because you hear directly from the person. Records review and surveys give data collected by others. Interviews allow clarification, deeper probing, and understanding context — making the information richer and more personal.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The ECOLOGICAL APPROACH in community diagnosis focuses on:
options: Only the physical environment of the community
Community features, health indices, and health resources altogether
Clinical findings from individual patient records
Environmental pollution levels only
Hospital admission rates

rationale.text: The ecological approach is holistic — it looks at the WHOLE picture: community features (demographics, sociocultural, political, economic), health indices (IMR, MMR, morbidity), and health resources (essential services, PHC elements). It identifies health problems AND the factors causing them.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Which of the following is a PURPOSE of community diagnosis according to WHO?
options: To replace the function of the rural health unit
To identify, determine, and set priorities for planning health actions
To prescribe medications to the sick in the community
To conduct mass vaccination campaigns only
To collect taxes for health programs

rationale.text: WHO states that community diagnosis aims to: DEFINE existing problems, IDENTIFY available resources, and SET priorities for planning, implementing, and evaluating health actions. Know the problem → find your tools → plan what to do.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Which among the following is a GUIDING PRINCIPLE of community diagnosis?
options: The assessment should only involve health professionals
The assessment should focus on specific information topics and is an ongoing process
Community participation should be minimized to avoid bias
Only quantitative data should be collected
The assessment should be conducted only once per year

rationale.text: Key guiding principles: the vision statement should guide the assessment, it should focus on SPECIFIC information topics, and assessment is an ONGOING process — not a one-time event. Community participation, not exclusion, is also a core principle.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: 'Additional Information Needed' in community diagnosis includes which of the following methods?
options: Physical examination of all residents
Surveys, Focus Group Discussions, Public Meetings and Forums, Interviews
Analysis of existing census data only
Laboratory tests for all community members
Review of hospital records only

rationale.text: When existing data is insufficient, additional information is gathered through Surveys, Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), Public Meetings and Forums, and Interviews. These participatory methods gather primary data directly from community members.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: 'Community mobilization' in community diagnosis is defined as:
options: Distributing medicines to community members
Transforming awareness into collective action, planning achievable early wins
Mobilizing military forces for disaster response
Relocating community members to safer areas
Enforcing health regulations through penalties

rationale.text: Community mobilization means: transforming awareness into collective action, planning achievable early wins to build momentum, engaging the broader community in implementation, and celebrating successes together. It converts knowledge into community-driven change.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Health Promotion is BEST defined as:
options: The prevention of communicable diseases only
The process of enabling people to increase control over their health
Providing free medicines to indigent populations
Enforcing health laws and regulations in the community
Conducting annual medical-surgical missions

rationale.text: WHO's definition: Health Promotion is 'the process of ENABLING people to INCREASE CONTROL over and to IMPROVE their health and its determinants.' The key idea is giving people the POWER to help themselves — not doing it FOR them.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: According to the Social Ecological Model of Health (SEMoF), what percentage of health outcomes is attributed to multi-sectoral factors?

rationale.text: The SEMoF formula: 80% of health is determined by MULTI-SECTORAL factors (education, employment, environment, social support), and only 20% by the health sector itself. This explains why doctors alone cannot make a community healthy — education, housing, and economic policies matter MORE.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The Ottawa Charter for Health Promotion (1986) includes which action areas?
options: Diagnosing diseases, prescribing medications, monitoring vital signs
Developing healthy public policies, creating supportive environments
Administering vaccines, distributing medicines, conducting surgery
Enforcing quarantine, isolating patients, treating infections
Collecting taxes, building roads, establishing schools

rationale.text: The Ottawa Charter has 5 action areas: (1) Develop healthy public policy, (2) Create supportive environments, (3) Strengthen community action, (4) Develop personal skills, (5) Reorient health services. These go far beyond hospitals — they involve policy, community, and personal empowerment.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: In the Health Impact Pyramid (CDC), which level has the LARGEST impact on population health?
options: Clinical interventions
Long-lasting protective interventions
Counseling and education
Changing the context to make default decisions healthy
Socioeconomic factors

rationale.text: Socioeconomic factors at the BASE of the Health Impact Pyramid have the LARGEST impact because they affect the most people simultaneously. Changing context (built environment, policies) is next, then protective interventions (vaccines), then clinical care at the top — which affects fewer people.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The DOH's shared vision for a Healthy Pilipinas by 2030 includes which THREE key strategies?
options: Vaccination, nutrition, and sanitation
Healthy Governance, Healthy Settings, and Health Literacy
Free medicines, free consultations, and free hospitalizations
Disease surveillance, outbreak response, and quarantine
Curative care, rehabilitative care, and palliative care

rationale.text: Healthy Pilipinas rests on 3 pillars: (1) HEALTHY GOVERNANCE — policies and leadership; (2) HEALTHY SETTINGS — promoting health where people live, work, and learn; (3) HEALTH LITERACY — enabling Filipinos to understand and act on health information.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: SBCC stands for:
options: Social Behavior Change Communication
Systems-Based Community Care
Situational-Based Clinical Communication
Social-Based Community Coordination
Strategic Behavior and Communication Capacity

rationale.text: SBCC = Social and Behavioral Change Communication. It is a strategy that uses communication and social approaches to CHANGE BEHAVIORS — not just increase knowledge. The goal is to move people from awareness → attitude change → behavior change → social norm change.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: In SBCC, what does DIKAR stand for?
options: Data, Information, Knowledge, Action, Results
Design, Implementation, Key Audiences, Resources
Determine, Identify, Key, Assess, Resolve
Diagnosis, Intervention, Key, Analysis, Review
Data, Index, Knowledge, Advocacy, Resources

rationale.text: DIKAR = Data → Information → Knowledge → Action → Results. It's the logical flow of SBCC: raw DATA becomes meaningful INFORMATION, builds KNOWLEDGE, that knowledge drives ACTION, and action produces RESULTS (better health outcomes).

subject: Family & Community Health
question: RAKID is the reverse of DIKAR and is used to:
options: Design communication messages from scratch
Plan backward from desired RESULTS to identify what DATA is needed
Evaluate the effectiveness of health programs
Conduct community needs assessment
Train barangay health workers

rationale.text: RAKID = Results → Action → Knowledge → Information → Data. You start with the end in mind (what results do you want?), then work BACKWARD to figure out: what actions are needed? what knowledge must people have? what data will you collect? It's backward planning.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The COM-B Diagnostic Tool assesses barriers to behavior change. COM-B stands for:
options: Community, Organization, Management, Behavior
Capability, Opportunity, Motivation, Behavior
Communication, Objectives, Methods, Budget
Comprehension, Observation, Measurement, Baseline
Community, Outcome, Monitoring, Behavior

rationale.text: COM-B = Capability + Opportunity + Motivation → Behavior. For any behavior change: does the person have CAPABILITY (physical/psychological ability)? OPPORTUNITY (environment, resources, social norms)? MOTIVATION (intrinsic/extrinsic desire)? All three must align for behavior change to happen.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A health team wants to reduce smoking in a factory. Workers KNOW smoking is harmful but continue because 'everyone does it.' Using COM-B, which barrier is MOST prominent?
options: Capability — they lack the physical ability to quit
Motivation — they don't want to quit
Opportunity — social norms make quitting difficult
Capability — they lack knowledge about smoking's dangers
Motivation — they have no intrinsic desire to be healthy

rationale.text: When people KNOW the problem but continue because 'everyone does it,' the barrier is OPPORTUNITY — specifically SOCIAL NORMS. The COM-B solution is to change the social norm (e.g., smoke-free workplace policy) rather than just re-educating people.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The 'Institutional Level' of Healthy Behaviors in the Community refers to:
options: Knowledge and attitudes of individuals
Family and neighbor influence
Community norms and traditions
Laws and policies, enforcement, and media
Access to primary health care services only

rationale.text: The community has 4 levels of influence: Individual (knowledge/attitudes), Interpersonal (family/friends), Community (norms/culture), and INSTITUTIONAL (laws, policies, enforcement, media, resources). Institutional factors shape the rules everyone lives by.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The FOUR PRINCIPLES of a Healthy Pilipinas are:
options: Quality, Safety, Access, Equity
Equity, Participation, Partnerships, Responsiveness
Prevention, Promotion, Protection, Provision
Awareness, Attitude, Behavior, Culture
Leadership, Governance, Policy, Implementation

rationale.text: The 4 principles: EQUITY (address health disparities), PARTICIPATION (involve people in decisions), PARTNERSHIPS (collaborate across sectors), and RESPONSIVENESS (adapt to population needs). These guide how health promotion is done in the Philippines.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Human Centered Design Thinking in health promotion is BEST described as:
options: Designing health systems based on government budget priorities
A creative approach to problem solving centered on the people you're designing for
A clinical method for diagnosing diseases
An engineering approach to hospital construction
A method for ranking diseases by severity

rationale.text: Human Centered Design starts with EMPATHY — deeply understanding the people affected. You design WITH them, not FOR them, and you test solutions based on their actual needs, not assumptions. In health, this makes interventions more relevant, accepted, and effective.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A KEY BENEFIT STATEMENT in SBCC should answer which question from the target audience's perspective?
options: How much does this program cost?
What's in it for me? How does this help me?
Who is funding this health campaign?
What disease does this prevent?
Who is the target population?

rationale.text: The key benefit statement answers 'WHAT'S IN IT FOR ME?' from the audience's perspective. People are motivated by PERSONAL BENEFITS, not medical facts. A good benefit statement clearly communicates how taking action will improve THEIR life.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Health Literacy, as a key strategy of the Health Promotion Framework, means:
options: The ability to read and write health-related textbooks
The ability of individuals to obtain, process, and understand basic health information
The number of health professionals per population
The percentage of the population with health insurance
The ability of hospitals to provide quality care

rationale.text: Health Literacy is the capacity to FIND, UNDERSTAND, and USE health information to make good decisions. It's more than reading — it includes understanding prescriptions, navigating health systems, evaluating health information online, and knowing when to seek care.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Healthy Settings in the Philippine context include:
options: Only hospitals and clinics
Healthy Communities, Healthy Schools, Healthy Workplaces, and Healthy Hospitals
Only government offices and schools
Only Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas
Only barangay health centers

rationale.text: Healthy Settings include: Healthy Communities, Healthy Schools (using the 6-component framework: policy, physical environment, social environment, community links, health skills, health care), Healthy Workplaces, and Healthy Hospitals. Every place where Filipinos live, learn, and work should promote health.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A DOH team is designing a hand-washing campaign. Mothers in a rural barangay know hand-washing is important but don't do it before feeding their children. Which SBCC step should they do FIRST?
options: Design communication materials immediately
Conduct audience analysis to understand the specific barriers
Launch a social media campaign
Distribute free soap to all households
Train barangay health workers to demonstrate hand washing

rationale.text: Before designing any message or material, you must do AUDIENCE ANALYSIS — understand WHO your audience is, what they know, what barriers they face, and what motivates them. Distributing soap helps, but if the real barrier is time or cultural norms, soap alone won't change behavior.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The Health Promotion Framework Strategy 2030 is governed by which Philippine Administrative Order?

rationale.text: Administrative Order 2021-0063 established the Health Promotion Framework Strategy 2030 — the DOH's blueprint for health promotion from 2021 to 2030. It defines the direction for planning, developing, and implementing health promotion policies in the Philippines.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A health promoter 'engineers the lifestyle of people.' This means they:
options: Prescribe medications to change health behaviors
Design strategies that make healthy choices easier and more accessible
Conduct surgery to prevent diseases
Monitor patients in the ICU
Enforce health regulations through fines

rationale.text: A health promoter DESIGNS environments, programs, and policies that SHAPE behavior toward healthy choices. Like an engineer designs a bridge to make crossing easy, a health promoter designs systems that make healthy living the easier, default choice.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A community has a Crude Birth Rate of 28 per 1,000 and a Crude Death Rate of 8 per 1,000. The rate of natural increase is:

rationale.text: Rate of Natural Increase = CBR − CDR = 28 − 8 = 20 per 1,000. Natural increase does NOT include migration — only births and deaths. A rate of 20/1,000 means the community is growing by 20 per year per 1,000 people from births alone.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The Five-Star Doctor concept was proposed as:
options: A ranking system for doctors based on years of experience
An ideal profile of a doctor with a mix of aptitudes to meet relevance, quality, cost-effectiveness
A grading system used by the Philippine Medical Association
A model exclusively for specialists in tertiary hospitals
A performance evaluation tool for government doctors

rationale.text: The Five-Star Doctor (WHO) is an IDEAL PROFILE — not a ranking or grade. It describes a doctor with the RIGHT MIX of roles and aptitudes to serve relevance, quality, cost-effectiveness, and equity. It's about being a COMPLETE physician, not just a clinician.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The FIVE roles of a Five-Star Doctor are:
options: Surgeon, Internist, Pediatrician, OB-Gyne, Psychiatrist
Care Provider, Decision-Maker, Communicator, Community Leader, Manager
Clinician, Educator, Researcher, Administrator, Advocate
Diagnostician, Prescriber, Surgeon, Counselor, Researcher
Healer, Teacher, Leader, Innovator, Diplomat

rationale.text: The 5 roles: (1) CARE PROVIDER — holistic patient care; (2) DECISION-MAKER — evidence-based, ethical decisions; (3) COMMUNICATOR — effective communication; (4) COMMUNITY LEADER — serves and advocates for the community; (5) MANAGER — manages resources and teams.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: 'Relevance' in the Five-Star Doctor framework refers to:
options: The financial cost of medical services
The degree to which the most important health problems are tackled
The quality of clinical skills demonstrated
The number of patients seen per day
The level of specialization of the physician

rationale.text: RELEVANCE = focusing on what MATTERS MOST to the population. It asks: 'Are we addressing the most important health problems?' A relevant doctor prioritizes the real needs of the community — not just interesting cases or profitable procedures.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: As a CARE PROVIDER, a Five-Star Doctor considers the patient as:
options: An isolated individual with physical symptoms only
An integral part of a family and community, with total physical, mental
A customer to be satisfied with minimal consultation time
A case study for medical research
A recipient of prescriptions and procedures

rationale.text: The Care Provider role is HOLISTIC and INTEGRATED. The patient is part of a FAMILY and COMMUNITY. Care should be continuous (ongoing), complementary (curative + preventive + rehabilitative working together), and of the HIGHEST quality.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: 'Equity' in the context of the Five-Star Doctor means:
options: All patients pay the same consultation fee
People's need, rather than social privilege
All doctors must see the same number of patients
Healthcare is free for everyone
Doctors must treat government officials with priority

rationale.text: EQUITY means distributing healthcare based on NEED, not wealth, status, or privilege. A Five-Star Doctor strives to make quality care accessible to ALL — especially the poor and marginalized — because health is a right, not a privilege.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Evidence-Based Medicine (EBM) in the 21st century is described as:
options: Relying solely on clinical experience without research evidence
Integration of best research evidence with clinical expertise and patient values
Using only the most expensive diagnostic tools available
Prescribing medications based on pharmaceutical company recommendations
Following protocols without considering individual patient circumstances

rationale.text: EBM = BEST RESEARCH EVIDENCE + CLINICAL EXPERTISE + PATIENT VALUES. All three must be integrated. Research alone ignores clinical judgment; clinical expertise alone ignores current evidence; both without patient values ignores patient autonomy.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A physician in a rural health unit notices high rates of dengue. She organizes a community clean-up drive, coordinates with local officials, and educates families about mosquito breeding sites. Which Five-Star Doctor roles is she PRIMARILY demonstrating?
options: Care Provider and Decision-Maker
Communicator and Community Leader
Manager and Researcher
Care Provider and Manager
Decision-Maker and Manager

rationale.text: By educating families (COMMUNICATOR) and organizing community action while coordinating with local officials (COMMUNITY LEADER), she demonstrates these two roles. She goes BEYOND the clinic to address health at the population level — exactly what a Five-Star Doctor does.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The Seven Fundamental Aspects of Medicine include all EXCEPT:
options: Medicine is based on communication
Medicine is linked to the divine
Medicine is inseparable from the rituals with which it is practiced
Medicine is exclusively a natural science with no humanistic components
Systems of healing evolve from shared cultural worldviews

rationale.text: All 7 aspects emphasize that medicine is BOTH science AND art, deeply human, cultural, ritual, communicative, trust-based, and spiritually connected. Medicine is NEVER 'exclusively' a natural science — that statement contradicts all 7 aspects.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: As a DECISION-MAKER, a Five-Star Doctor must:
options: Always follow the patient's wishes regardless of clinical appropriateness
Take decisions in a climate of transparency, considering ethical principles
Avoid making independent decisions and always consult specialists
Make decisions based primarily on the patient's ability to pay
Follow only hospital protocols without individualization

rationale.text: As a Decision-Maker, the Five-Star Doctor makes EVIDENCE-BASED, ETHICAL decisions in a climate of TRANSPARENCY. This means being honest about options, risks, and limitations, while upholding ethical principles (autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice).

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Medicine as an ART means:
options: Doctors should draw or paint as a hobby
Medicine deals with humans and their feelings, involves communication and philosophy
Medical procedures should be aesthetically designed
Hospital interiors should be artistically decorated
Doctors should be creative in writing prescriptions

rationale.text: Medicine as an ART recognizes that: patients are HUMANS with feelings (not just diseased organs), medicine is about COMMUNICATION and RELATIONSHIPS, it deals with the PHILOSOPHY of the human person, and integrates with other humanities and disciplines. Science + Art = Healing.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: 'Cost-effectiveness' in the Five-Star Doctor framework means:
options: Choosing the cheapest treatment available
Interventions with the greatest positive health impact for the resources used
Providing free services to all patients
Using generic medicines instead of branded ones
Avoiding diagnostic tests to reduce costs

rationale.text: COST-EFFECTIVENESS = GREATEST POSITIVE HEALTH IMPACT for the resources used. It's NOT about being cheap — it's about being EFFICIENT. A cost-effective intervention delivers the most health benefit per peso spent.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: As a MANAGER, the Five-Star Doctor:
options: Manages hospital finances and investments
Manages healthcare resources wisely, leads teams
Manages pharmaceutical supplies for resale
Handles hospital human resources and payroll
Manages patient bills and insurance claims only

rationale.text: As a Manager, the Five-Star Doctor uses SCARCE RESOURCES wisely — human, physical, financial. They lead healthcare teams, organize services for maximum effectiveness, and balance quality with cost-effectiveness. In a country with limited resources like the Philippines, this role is critical.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: As a COMMUNITY LEADER, the Five-Star Doctor:
options: Runs for political office to influence health legislation
Advocates for community health, participates in community programs
Focuses exclusively on hospital-based care
Delegates all community health activities to nurses and midwives
Only participates in health activities when required by the hospital

rationale.text: The Community Leader role means the doctor is ACTIVELY ENGAGED in the community — not just in the clinic. They advocate for health equity, participate in community health programs, and help mobilize collective action. A doctor who only stays in the clinic fulfills only ONE of the five roles.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The COMMUNICATOR role of a Five-Star Doctor involves:
options: Primarily writing prescriptions and referral letters
Effectively communicating with patients, families, colleagues
Using technical medical jargon to establish authority
Communicating only with other doctors in the healthcare team
Using social media to advertise medical services

rationale.text: The Communicator role means being able to communicate effectively with EVERYONE: patients (explaining diagnoses in understandable language), families (involving them in care), colleagues (coordinating care), and communities (health education and advocacy). Communication is THE core skill of healing.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The Researcher/Lifelong Learner role of the Five-Star Doctor involves:
options: Publishing research papers only in international journals
Using evidence-based medicine, choosing technology ethically
Conducting drug trials for pharmaceutical companies
Researching only in academic medical centers
Focusing on research to the exclusion of clinical practice

rationale.text: The Researcher/Lifelong Learner (often discussed as a 6th role) means using EBM in practice, choosing technology ETHICALLY and cost-effectively, and constantly UPDATING one's knowledge. In a rapidly evolving medical landscape, a doctor who stops learning becomes dangerous.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The THREE COMPONENTS of PHC according to WHO are:
options: Curative care, preventive care, and rehabilitative care
Primary care as the core of integrated health services, multisectoral policy and action
Free medicines, free hospitalization, and free surgery
Disease surveillance, outbreak response, and quarantine
Vaccination, nutrition, and sanitation

rationale.text: The 3 PHC components: (1) PRIMARY CARE + essential public health functions as the CORE of integrated services; (2) MULTISECTORAL POLICY AND ACTION — addressing determinants beyond health; (3) EMPOWERED PEOPLE AND COMMUNITIES — as advocates, co-developers, and self-carers. All three MUST work together.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The Alma-Ata Declaration was adopted in which year?

rationale.text: The Alma-Ata Declaration (1978) — jointly convened by WHO and UNICEF — proclaimed 'HEALTH FOR ALL BY THE YEAR 2000' through primary health care. It recognized that health equity requires going beyond hospitals to communities, families, and social determinants.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The Astana Declaration (2018) was significant because it:
options: Replaced the Alma-Ata Declaration entirely with a new framework
Reaffirmed global commitment to PHC with renewed emphasis on UHC and the SDGs
Abolished the concept of primary care globally
Focused exclusively on infectious disease control
Established the World Health Organization

rationale.text: Astana (2018) was a RENEWAL — it didn't replace Alma-Ata but REINFORCED it. It emphasized making PHC the cornerstone of achieving UHC and the SDGs, and updated strategies for the modern era. Both declarations are milestones of global commitment to PHC.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The 5 Cs of Primary Care are:
options: Curative, Chronic, Complex, Community, Comprehensive
First Contact, Comprehensiveness, Coordination, Continuity, Person-Centeredness
Clinical, Competent, Cost-effective, Collaborative, Compassionate
Care, Community, Capacity, Coverage, Control
Communication, Competence, Confidentiality, Compassion, Commitment

rationale.text: The 5 Cs: (1) FIRST CONTACT — first entry point into the health system; (2) COMPREHENSIVENESS — covers all health needs; (3) COORDINATION — links to other services; (4) CONTINUITY — ongoing relationship over time; (5) PERSON-CENTEREDNESS — treats the whole person, not just the disease.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Universal Health Coverage (UHC) means that ALL people have access to:
options: Free healthcare at all levels without any cost
Quality health services they need without suffering financial hardship
Specialist care at tertiary hospitals for free
All medications without prescription
Emergency care only

rationale.text: UHC = access to QUALITY health services WITHOUT FINANCIAL HARDSHIP. It does NOT mean everything is free — it means people are financially protected from catastrophic health expenses. The 3 UHC dimensions: who is covered, which services are covered, and how much of the cost is covered.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The Six Building Blocks of a Health System according to WHO are:
options: Doctors, Nurses, Pharmacists, Dentists, Midwives, and Barangay Health Workers
Service delivery, Health workforce, Health information, Medical products/vaccines/technologies, Financing, and Leadership/Governance
Hospitals, Clinics, Laboratories, Pharmacies, Ambulances, and Health Centers
Prevention, Promotion, Curative, Rehabilitative, Palliative, and Emergency care
National, Regional, Provincial, City, Municipal, and Barangay health offices

rationale.text: WHO's 6 Building Blocks: (1) SERVICE DELIVERY, (2) HEALTH WORKFORCE, (3) HEALTH INFORMATION SYSTEMS, (4) MEDICAL PRODUCTS/VACCINES/TECHNOLOGIES, (5) HEALTH FINANCING, and (6) LEADERSHIP/GOVERNANCE. All six must function well AND work together.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Which BEST distinguishes Primary Health Care from Primary Care?
options: Primary Health Care and Primary Care are identical concepts
Primary Health Care is a broader framework addressing the whole society
Primary Care is more comprehensive than Primary Health Care
Primary Health Care focuses only on clinical care at health centers
Primary Care is a policy approach while PHC is a clinical approach

rationale.text: KEY DISTINCTION: PHC = broad FRAMEWORK and APPROACH (society-level, multisectoral); PRIMARY CARE = specific LEVEL OF CARE (first-contact clinical services, framed by the 5Cs). Primary care is one COMPONENT of PHC.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: PHC Principle 1 states that PHC entails three inter-related and synergistic components. This means they:
options: Can work independently of each other
Are optional depending on government resources
Work together and strengthen each other
Are listed in order of priority
Are applicable only in developing countries

rationale.text: SYNERGISTIC = working TOGETHER, each making the others more powerful. You cannot have effective PHC with only clinical services and no multisectoral action; or with empowered communities but no health services. All three components are NECESSARY and INTERDEPENDENT.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A barangay health worker visits an elderly diabetic patient at home monthly, coordinates with the RHU doctor, and links the patient to PhilHealth for medicines. Which PHC principle is MOST demonstrated?
options: PHC focuses exclusively on acute care
PHC provides whole-person care for health needs throughout the lifespan
PHC is only applicable in urban areas
PHC requires specialist involvement in all cases
PHC is limited to preventive care only

rationale.text: This demonstrates WHOLE-PERSON CARE + CONTINUITY + COORDINATION. The BHW provides care at home (accessibility), links to the RHU (coordination), and connects to PhilHealth (coverage). This is PHC in action — integrated, person-centered, and continuous.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: 'Empowered People and Communities' in PHC means they serve as:
options: Passive recipients of health services
Advocates, co-developers of health services, and self-carers/caregivers
Voters for health-related politicians
Donors for hospital construction
Supervisors of health workers

rationale.text: Empowerment in PHC has THREE dimensions: (1) ADVOCATES — demanding their right to health; (2) CO-DEVELOPERS — actively participating in designing health services; (3) SELF-CARERS and CAREGIVERS — managing their own health and supporting family/community members.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The ROLE OF PHC WORKERS includes:
options: Performing surgery and specialist procedures
Health Care Provider, Health Educator, Social/Community Mobilizer, Researcher
Only providing medicines and vaccines
Only conducting disease surveillance
Administrative work only

rationale.text: PHC workers have FIVE roles: (1) HEALTH CARE PROVIDER; (2) HEALTH EDUCATOR; (3) SOCIAL/COMMUNITY MOBILIZER; (4) RESEARCHER — using evidence to improve care; (5) COORDINATOR for CONTINUITY OF CARE — ensuring patients move smoothly through the system.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: PHC requires governments to underscore the importance of 'action beyond the health sector' through:
options: Building more hospitals
A whole-of-government approach including health-in-all-policies
Privatizing health services
Increasing medicine importation
Restricting access to tertiary care

rationale.text: PHC Principle 3: health requires 'HEALTH IN ALL POLICIES' — meaning agriculture, education, housing, transportation, and economic policies must ALL consider their impact on health. A road without sidewalks harms health. Health is EVERYONE's business, not just the DOH's.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The Philippines' Universal Health Care Act (RA 11223) operationalizes UHC through:
options: Free hospitalization for all Filipinos at government hospitals
Health Care Provider Networks
Abolition of all health insurance premiums
Mandatory private health insurance for all workers
Free specialist consultations for all Filipino citizens

rationale.text: RA 11223 establishes HEALTH CARE PROVIDER NETWORKS (HCPNs) — integrated, province-wide or city-wide networks that link all levels of care. A Health Care Coordinator ensures continuity and navigation. This replaces fragmented, facility-centric care with integrated, population-based care.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The Philippines has a significant 'brain drain' of nurses going abroad. Which Health System Building Block does this MOST directly affect?
options: Health Financing
Medical Products and Technologies
Health Workforce
Service Delivery
Leadership and Governance

rationale.text: Brain drain of nurses directly weakens the HEALTH WORKFORCE building block — the most critical resource in healthcare. Without enough nurses, service delivery collapses, quality of care declines, and health information is poorly managed.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: PHC is described as a framework that addresses the 'BROADER DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH.' This includes:
options: Only biological and genetic factors
Physical, mental, and social health and well-being
Only infectious disease determinants
Only environmental pollution factors
Only genetic predispositions to disease

rationale.text: PHC Principle 4: PHC addresses the BROADER DETERMINANTS — physical health, mental health, social well-being, AND socioeconomic circumstances. This aligns with WHO's definition of health: 'complete physical, mental, and social well-being.'

subject: Family & Community Health
question: PHC is BEST defined as:
options: A specific level of care provided only at health centers
A whole-of-society approach to health through three synergistic components
A program exclusively for infectious disease control
Free healthcare provided by the government
An emergency response system for disease outbreaks

rationale.text: PHC is a WHOLE-OF-SOCIETY approach — meaning it involves government, communities, individuals, and all sectors (not just health). Its three components: (1) primary care as the core, (2) multisectoral policy and action, and (3) empowered people and communities.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: PHC provides whole-person care for health needs throughout the lifespan, not just for a set of specific diseases. This is PHC Principle:
options: Principle 1
Principle 2
Principle 3
Principle 4
Principle 5

rationale.text: PHC Principle 5 states that PHC provides WHOLE-PERSON CARE for health needs THROUGHOUT THE LIFESPAN — from promotion to prevention to diagnosis to treatment to rehabilitation to palliative care. It is not limited to any specific disease or life stage.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: PHC ensures people receive quality comprehensive care as CLOSE AS FEASIBLE to people's everyday environment. This relates to which PHC Principle?
options: Principle 1
Principle 2
Principle 3
Principle 4
Principle 6

rationale.text: PHC Principle 6: PHC ensures quality comprehensive care — ranging from promotion and prevention to treatment, rehabilitation, and palliative care — AS CLOSE AS FEASIBLE to people's everyday environment. This emphasizes accessibility and community-based care delivery.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Which statement CORRECTLY describes the relationship between PHC and Universal Health Coverage?
options: PHC and UHC are opposing concepts
PHC is the FOUNDATION and primary vehicle for achieving UHC
UHC can be achieved without PHC
PHC is only relevant to low-income countries
UHC is a prerequisite for PHC implementation

rationale.text: PHC is the FOUNDATION for achieving UHC. Strong primary care prevents unnecessary hospitalization, catches diseases early, manages chronic conditions — all at lower cost. Countries with strong PHC systems consistently achieve better UHC outcomes.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The HEALTH FINANCING building block aims to:
options: Collect taxes for government spending
Ensure adequate funds are raised, used efficiently
Manage pharmaceutical company profits
Determine doctor salaries
Build and maintain hospital infrastructure

rationale.text: Health Financing has THREE functions: (1) REVENUE COLLECTION — raising funds; (2) POOLING — sharing financial risk across populations; (3) PURCHASING — paying for services effectively. The ultimate goal: ensure people can use health services WITHOUT FINANCIAL RUIN.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A RATE in vital statistics BEST refers to:
options: A simple count of events in a population
The relationship between a vital event and the population at risk, over time
A ratio of two unrelated populations
A percentage of disease in a community
A measurement of hospital capacity

rationale.text: A RATE has THREE components: (1) numerator = people who EXPERIENCED the event; (2) denominator = people EXPOSED TO THE RISK; (3) a TIME period. The denominator must include only those at risk. This distinguishes rates from simple counts or general ratios.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The CRUDE BIRTH RATE (CBR) is calculated as:
options: Total deaths ÷ Total population × 1,000
Total live births ÷ Estimated midyear population × 1,000
Total pregnancies ÷ Women of reproductive age × 1,000
Total live births ÷ Total women × 1,000
Neonatal deaths ÷ Live births × 1,000

rationale.text: CBR = (Total live births registered ÷ Estimated midyear population) × 1,000. 'Crude' means it uses the TOTAL population as the denominator. The midyear population (July 1 estimate) best represents the average population exposed throughout the year.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The INFANT MORTALITY RATE (IMR) is calculated as:
options: Deaths under 28 days ÷ Live births × 1,000
Deaths under 1 year ÷ Total registered live births of the same year × 1,000
Deaths under 5 years ÷ Total population × 1,000
Maternal deaths ÷ Live births × 1,000
Stillbirths ÷ Total pregnancies × 1,000

rationale.text: IMR = (Deaths under 1 year ÷ Total live births of the same year) × 1,000. The IMR is one of the MOST IMPORTANT health indicators because it reflects the overall health and environmental conditions — sanitation, nutrition, access to care, and maternal health all directly affect infant survival.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Why is the Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) considered a SENSITIVE index of community health?
options: Because it is easy to calculate
Because it reflects changes in environmental, medical, and social conditions
Because it is the most commonly reported statistic
Because it measures adult mortality
Because it is required by the WHO

rationale.text: Infants are EXTREMELY vulnerable to environmental, nutritional, and medical conditions. High IMR means poor sanitation, malnutrition, inadequate prenatal care, or poor access to medical services. When a community improves its health programs, the IMR drops quickly — making it a SENSITIVE indicator of real change.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The NEONATAL DEATH RATE (NDR) measures deaths occurring:
options: From birth to 1 year of age
During the first 28 days of life, expressed per 1,000 live births
From 1 month to 1 year of age
From 1 to 5 years of age
During the perinatal period only

rationale.text: NDR = (Deaths under 28 days of age ÷ Total live births of the same year) × 1,000. The neonatal period (first 28 days) is when babies are most vulnerable to conditions related to birth — prematurity, birth asphyxia, infections. NDR is an index of the quality of PRENATAL CARE and OBSTETRICAL MANAGEMENT.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The MATERNAL MORTALITY RATE (MMR) is an index of:
options: Overall community health conditions
Obstetrical care needed and received by women in a community
Neonatal health outcomes
Infectious disease burden in women
Fertility rate of the population

rationale.text: MMR = (Maternal deaths related to pregnancy, childbirth, and puerperium ÷ Total live births of the same year) × 1,000. It specifically measures the RISK OF DYING FROM PREGNANCY-RELATED CAUSES and serves as an index of the QUALITY AND AVAILABILITY OF OBSTETRICAL CARE.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A SPECIFIC RATE differs from a CRUDE RATE in that it:
options: Uses a larger denominator
Limits the event to a portion of the specifically exposed population
Is only used for infectious diseases
Is calculated monthly instead of annually
Always uses 100,000 as the multiplier

rationale.text: SPECIFIC RATES refine the analysis by focusing on a SPECIFIC GROUP — those truly exposed to the risk. Examples: Age-Specific Death Rate, Sex-Specific Death Rate, Cause-Specific Death Rate. Specific rates are MORE INFORMATIVE than crude rates because they control for confounding factors.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The GENERAL FERTILITY RATE (GFR) is calculated as:
options: Live births ÷ Total population × 1,000
Live births ÷ Women of childbearing age × 1,000
Total pregnancies ÷ Total women × 1,000
Live births ÷ Married women × 1,000
Total births ÷ Total men × 1,000

rationale.text: GFR = (Live births ÷ Women of childbearing age 15–49) × 1,000. Unlike the Crude Birth Rate (which uses the TOTAL population), the GFR uses ONLY WOMEN AT RISK of childbearing as the denominator — making it a more accurate measure of actual fertility.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The TOTAL FERTILITY RATE (TFR) represents:
options: The average number of children born to all women in a country
The average live births a woman would have across her entire reproductive life
The ratio of births to deaths in a year
The number of pregnancies per 1,000 women
The number of live births per 1,000 married women

rationale.text: TFR = the average number of children a woman would have over her ENTIRE REPRODUCTIVE LIFE (ages 15–49) if current age-specific fertility rates remained constant. TFR of 2.1 = 'replacement level.' TFR > 2.1 = population growth; TFR < 2.1 = potential population decline.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: In Barangay Luntian, there were 120 live births and 3 maternal deaths in 2024. The Maternal Mortality Rate is:
options: 0.3 per 1,000 live births
25 per 1,000 live births
3 per 1,000 midyear population
2.5 per 1,000 women of reproductive age
0.03 per 1,000 population

rationale.text: MMR = (Maternal deaths ÷ Live births) × 1,000 = (3 ÷ 120) × 1,000 = 25 per 1,000 live births. REMEMBER: MMR uses LIVE BIRTHS as the denominator (not total population or women). The trap answer is using total population as denominator — that's wrong.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: In 2024, Barangay Maayos registered 500 live births and 15 deaths of infants under 1 year. The Infant Mortality Rate is:
options: 0.6 per 1,000 population
30 per 1,000 live births
15 per 1,000 midyear population
60 per 1,000 women
3 per 100 births

rationale.text: IMR = (Deaths under 1 year ÷ Total live births of the same year) × 1,000 = (15 ÷ 500) × 1,000 = 30 per 1,000 live births. KEY: use LIVE BIRTHS as the denominator, NOT total population.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The CHILD/WOMEN RATIO is calculated as:
options: Number of children under 5 ÷ Total population × 100
Living children aged 0–4 years ÷ Women of childbearing age
Number of children in school ÷ Total women × 1,000
Children under 15 ÷ Women aged 15–49
Number of births ÷ Women aged 20–44

rationale.text: Child/Women Ratio = (Living children 0–4 years) ÷ (Women of childbearing age 15–44). This is a SIMPLE MEASURE of recent fertility — useful when birth registration is incomplete. More living young children relative to reproductive-age women = higher recent fertility.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The GROSS REPRODUCTION RATE (GRR) is defined as:
options: Number of live births per 1,000 population
The average number of daughters a newborn girl will bear during her lifetime
The average number of all children per woman
The ratio of daughters born to total births
The number of women who survive to reproductive age

rationale.text: GRR = average number of DAUGHTERS a newborn girl will bear in her lifetime, assuming FIXED age-specific fertility rates — but ignoring mortality (assuming she survives). The limitation: it assumes zero mortality, which is unrealistic.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: An Age-Specific Death Rate is calculated as:
options: All deaths ÷ Total population × 1,000
Deaths in a specific age group ÷ Population in that same age group × 1,000
Deaths from a specific disease ÷ Total population × 1,000
Deaths of a specific sex ÷ Total population × 1,000
Maternal deaths ÷ Live births × 1,000

rationale.text: Age-Specific Death Rate = (Deaths in a specific age group ÷ Estimated population in THAT SAME age group) × 1,000. This is more informative than the crude death rate because it compares populations at similar biological risk, revealing if young adults, elderly, or children are disproportionately dying.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Which vital statistic is MOST useful as an index of prenatal care quality and obstetrical management of the newborn?
options: Crude Birth Rate
Infant Mortality Rate
Neonatal Death Rate
Maternal Mortality Rate
Fetal Death Rate

rationale.text: The NEONATAL DEATH RATE (first 28 days) is the BEST index of prenatal care quality and obstetrical management. Most neonatal deaths are caused by conditions present at or around birth: prematurity, birth asphyxia, congenital anomalies, and neonatal sepsis — all preventable with good prenatal and delivery care.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The PREGNANCY RATE is defined as:
options: Number of live births per 1,000 women
Ratio of all pregnancies to the number of women of reproductive age
Number of married women who become pregnant per year
Number of first-time pregnancies per 1,000 women
Total pregnancies minus abortion per 1,000 women

rationale.text: Pregnancy Rate = ALL PREGNANCIES (live births + stillbirths + abortions + still ongoing) ÷ Women of reproductive age. It captures the TOTAL fertility experience — including pregnancies that don't end in live births. It is broader than the birth rate.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A RATIO in vital statistics describes:
options: The relationship between a vital event and the population at risk, within a specific time period
The relationship between two quantities without necessarily considering time or exposure to risk
An age-adjusted measure of mortality
A standardized measure of disease frequency
A measure of disease incidence in a specific population

rationale.text: A RATIO simply compares two numbers — the numerator and denominator do NOT need to represent the same entities or time period. A RATE requires that the numerator comes FROM the denominator (people at risk). Ratios are more general; rates are more specific.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The CAUSE-SPECIFIC DEATH RATE is calculated as:
options: All deaths ÷ Total population × 1,000
Deaths from a specific cause ÷ Estimated midyear population × 1,000
Deaths in a specific age group ÷ Population in that age group × 1,000
Deaths of a specific sex ÷ Population of that sex × 1,000
Maternal deaths ÷ Live births × 1,000

rationale.text: Cause-Specific Death Rate = (Deaths from a specific cause ÷ Estimated midyear population) × 1,000. This helps identify which diseases are KILLING THE MOST PEOPLE in a community, guiding resource allocation and program priorities.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A community health officer notes that the local IMR has decreased from 45 to 18 per 1,000 live births over 10 years following a maternal-child health program. This change MOST likely indicates:
options: A decrease in the crude birth rate
Improvement in environmental, medical
An increase in the total fertility rate
A decrease in the maternal mortality rate only
Improvement in adult health outcomes

rationale.text: A DROP in IMR from 45 to 18 reflects REAL IMPROVEMENT in the factors that keep infants alive: better sanitation, improved nutrition, increased breastfeeding, better prenatal care, accessible immunizations, and trained health workers. A decreasing IMR is one of the strongest signs that health programs are WORKING.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A region reports 200 tuberculosis deaths in 2024, with a midyear population of 400,000. The Cause-Specific Death Rate for TB is:

rationale.text: Cause-Specific Death Rate = (200 ÷ 400,000) × 1,000 = 0.5 per 1,000 (also expressed as 50 per 100,000 — how TB rates are commonly reported). This means for every 1,000 people, 0.5 died from TB — useful for comparing TB burden across regions.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Which vital rates use the ESTIMATED MIDYEAR POPULATION (July 1) as the denominator, and why?
options: Only the Infant Mortality Rate
The Crude Birth Rate and Crude Death Rate
Only the Maternal Mortality Rate
Only cause-specific death rates
Only age-specific rates for the elderly

rationale.text: The CBR and CDR use MIDYEAR POPULATION because population changes throughout the year. The JULY 1 ESTIMATE represents the MIDPOINT of the year — the best approximation of the average population at risk during that entire year.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A Sex-Specific Death Rate is computed as:
options: Deaths of a specific cause ÷ Total population × 1,000
Deaths of a specific sex ÷ Estimated population of that same sex × 1,000
Total deaths ÷ Total women × 1,000
Male deaths ÷ Female population × 1,000
Deaths in males under 65 ÷ Total male population × 1,000

rationale.text: Sex-Specific Death Rate = (Deaths of a specific sex ÷ Estimated population of THAT SAME sex) × 1,000. This tells you if men or women are dying at higher rates, helping plan gender-targeted interventions.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The FETAL DEATH RATE measures:
options: Deaths of newborns in the first week of life
Death of the product of conception before complete expulsion
Deaths of mothers during childbirth
Deaths of infants from infectious diseases
Deaths of children under 5 years of age

rationale.text: Fetal death (stillbirth) = death of the product of conception BEFORE complete expulsion, regardless of weeks of pregnancy. It measures PREGNANCY WASTAGE — how many pregnancies end in fetal death rather than live births, reflecting conditions like maternal infections, placental problems, and genetic abnormalities.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The CRUDE DEATH RATE (CDR) measures:
options: Deaths among children under 5 only
Mortality from all causes in the total population
Deaths from a specific disease only
Maternal deaths per live births
Deaths in the first month of life

rationale.text: CDR = (Total deaths from ALL causes ÷ Midyear population) × 1,000. 'Crude' means it applies to the ENTIRE population, regardless of age, sex, or cause. It measures the overall risk of dying in a given year and reflects the general mortality burden of a community.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: How does a RATIO differ from a RATE in vital statistics?
options: A ratio is always expressed per 1,000 population
The relationship between two quantities without requiring exposure to risk
A ratio and rate are identical in epidemiology
A ratio always uses the midyear population as its denominator
A ratio only applies to mortality data

rationale.text: A RATIO simply compares two numbers — the numerator and denominator do NOT need to represent the same entities or time period. Example: maternal mortality RATIO. A RATE requires the numerator to come FROM the denominator (people at risk). Ratios are more general; rates are more specific.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The Filipino Family is described as 'externally patriarchal, internally matriarchal.' This means:
options: The father makes all decisions inside and outside the home
The father is the public head, but the mother holds authority within the home
The mother is the legal head of the family
Authority is shared equally at all times
The eldest child holds authority in the absence of parents

rationale.text: 'Externally patriarchal' means the father is the publicly recognized head; 'internally matriarchal' means the mother actually runs the household and exerts significant influence over family decisions. This dual structure is a defining characteristic of the Filipino family.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The BIOLOGIC function of the family includes:
options: Provision of adequate financial resources
Reproduction, child rearing, nutrition, health maintenance, and recreation
Teaching skills, attitudes, and values
Socialization of children
Promoting the natural development of personalities

rationale.text: The BIOLOGIC function of the family covers: Reproduction, Child rearing/caring, Nutrition, Health maintenance, and Recreation. These are the basic biological activities that ensure the survival and physical well-being of family members.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: According to Doherty and McCubbin (1985), the family plays important roles in health of its members. These include all EXCEPT:
options: Health promotion and maintenance
Coping with stressful life events
Replacing the function of hospitals
Family-based health and illness appraisal
Family adaptation and coping with illness including care giving

rationale.text: Doherty and McCubbin identified: health promotion/maintenance, coping with stress, family-based health appraisal, family interaction in response to illness, help-seeking decisions, and family adaptation/coping. Replacing hospitals is NOT one of these roles — families COMPLEMENT health care, not replace it.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: 'The family is the greatest ally in the patient's treatment' is supported by which statistic?
options: 100% of cases require hospitalization
90% of cases are outpatient consultations managed at home
50% of diseases are treated at home
Only 10% of patients need family support
80% of diseases are communicable

rationale.text: 90% of cases are AMBULATORY — outpatient consultations with home confinement and prescriptions. This means the family is present for 90% of all care episodes, making it the most important ally in treatment compliance, recovery, and lifestyle modification.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The COMMUTER MARRIAGE is defined as:
options: A marriage where both partners work from home
A voluntary arrangement where dual-career couples maintain two separate residences
A marriage where one partner travels for work daily
A long-distance relationship before marriage
A marriage between two people from different cities

rationale.text: Commuter marriage: voluntary arrangement where dual-career couples maintain TWO RESIDENCES in different geographic locations, separated at LEAST THREE NIGHTS PER WEEK for a MINIMUM OF THREE MONTHS. It differs from regular long-distance relationships in its voluntary, structured nature.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Which type of family is composed of a group of individuals formed for specific ideological or societal purposes?
options: Nuclear family
Extended family
Blended family
Communal family
Single parent family

rationale.text: A COMMUNAL FAMILY is composed of a group of individuals formed for specific ideological or societal purposes. It is considered an alternative lifestyle for people who feel alienated from the predominantly economically-oriented society. It varies within social context.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: A family where the father is working in the UAE, the mother cares for their children in the Philippines, and there are no grandparents living with them. What is this family structure?
options: Nuclear family
Extended family
Single parent family
Blended family
Communal family

rationale.text: This is a SINGLE PARENT FAMILY because one parent is working outside the Philippines (OFW/DHW). The definition includes children living with only one parent — whether due to death, separation, or one parent working abroad. The absent parent doesn't make it nuclear; it functions as a single-parent unit.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: JOINT FAMILIES are families consisting of:
options: Parents and their dependent children only
Two or more married couples of the SAME generation
Three or more generations living together
Step-parents and step-children
Individuals with no blood relation living together

rationale.text: Joint families consist of two or more married couples (or divorced persons, widows, or widowers) of the SAME generation. This distinguishes them from extended families which include multiple GENERATIONS.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Which social change in the Filipino family is associated with KINSHIP TIES?
options: Increased authority of the father
Decreased social interaction among kinsmen leading to psychiatric disorders
Increase in extended family size
Greater community cohesion
More time for family activities

rationale.text: Weakened kinship ties (due to urbanization, migration, mass media, occupational specialization) have led to: less time for strong bonds, decreased social interaction, psychiatric disorders, and communication gaps. When kinship ties weaken, family members become more prone to illnesses due to decreased social support.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The NUCLEAR FAMILY is BEST described as:
options: Three generations living together
Parents and their still-dependent children
A family with step-parents and step-children
Two or more married couples of the same generation
A group formed for ideological purposes

rationale.text: The NUCLEAR FAMILY = parents and their STILL-DEPENDENT children in a SEPARATE dwelling not shared with either spouse's family of origin. The household is economically independent, subsisting on the occupational earnings of the husband/father. It is the BASIC UNIT from which all other forms evolve.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: According to Smilkstein (1978), the family is defined as:
options: A social group characterized by common residence, economic cooperation, and reproduction
Adult partners with and without children and single parents with children who function in a setting where there is a sense of home
A group of people related by blood, marriages or adoption, which live together in one household
A small social system made up of individuals related to each other by reason of strong reciprocal affections and loyalties
That social unit whose primary tasks are socialization of children and the stabilization of adult personalities

rationale.text: Smilkstein (1978) defined the family as: Adult partners with/without children AND single parents with children who function in a setting with a SENSE OF HOME and who have an agreement to establish NURTURING RELATIONSHIPS. This definition is notably inclusive and functional rather than purely structural.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The PSYCHOLOGIC/AFFECTION function of the family:
options: Provides adequate financial resources
Promotes natural development of personalities and psychological protection
Teaches skills relating to family functions
Provides reproductive and child-rearing functions
Socializes children into society

rationale.text: The PSYCHOLOGIC/AFFECTION function: (1) Promotes natural development of personalities; (2) Offers optimum psychological protection; (3) Promotes ability to form relationships with people in the family circle. This is the emotional and psychological foundation that the family provides to each member.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: 'FRAGILITY OF MARRIAGE' as a social change in the Filipino family is primarily due to:
options: Increased poverty and unemployment
Shift from utilitarian mate selection to emphasis on romantic relationships
Increased number of overseas Filipino workers
Government policies promoting divorce
Declining religious observance

rationale.text: Marriage fragility stems from: the shift from utilitarian basis (economic arrangement by kin) to SENTIMENTAL/SELF-REALIZATION basis. When emotional satisfaction is not found, the marriage crumbles. Additionally, social pressure to stay together has weakened — young people are more independent and laws are more relaxed.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: In the Philippine Constitution, which Article and Section states: 'The state recognizes the Filipino Family as the foundation of the nation'?
options: Article II Section 12
Article II Section 15
Article XIII Section 2
Article XV Section 1
Article XIV Section 3

rationale.text: Article XV Section 1 states: 'The state recognizes the Filipino Family as the foundation of the nation. Accordingly, it shall strengthen its solidarity and actively promote its total development.' This is the constitutional basis for family-centered health care and social policy in the Philippines.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Among the listed FAMILY STRENGTHS, which refers to the family members' ability to 'fill in' for one another during times of illness or when needed?
options: Growth-Producing Relationships
Self-help and Accepting Help
Flexibility of family functions and roles
Crisis as a means of growth
Family unity, Loyalty and Intra-family Cooperation

rationale.text: 'FLEXIBILITY OF FAMILY FUNCTIONS AND ROLES' refers to family members' ability to 'fill in' for one another during times of illness or when needed. This adaptability is crucial when a primary caregiver, breadwinner, or decision-maker is temporarily unavailable.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The REGENERATIVE FAMILY is BEST characterized by:
options: High family time and routines; high valuing of family time
High family flexibility and high family bonding
High family hardiness and high family coherence
Low family coherence and high family hardiness
Low family hardiness and high family bonding

rationale.text: The Regenerative Family (McCubbins) = HIGH FAMILY HARDINESS (internal strengths and durability) + HIGH FAMILY COHERENCE (emphasis on acceptance, loyalty, pride, faith, trust, respect, caring, and shared values). These families cope by working together to solve problems and feel in control of their circumstances.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The RHYTHMIC FAMILY is characterized by:
options: High family hardiness and high family coherence
High family flexibility and high family bonding
High family time and routines AND high valuing of family time and routines
Low flexibility and high bonding
High coherence and low hardiness

rationale.text: The Rhythmic Family = HIGH FAMILY TIME AND ROUTINES + HIGH VALUING OF FAMILY TIME AND ROUTINES. These families have a shared sense of purpose through regularity and predictability. They maintain continuity and stability through specific family activities repeated on a routine basis.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The VERSATILE FAMILY is characterized by:
options: High family hardiness and high family coherence
High family flexibility AND high family bonding
High family time and routines only
Low flexibility and high bonding
High coherence and low hardiness

rationale.text: The Versatile Family = HIGH FAMILY FLEXIBILITY (ability to change rules, boundaries, and roles to accommodate changing pressures) + HIGH FAMILY BONDING. These families can say what they want, give input into major decisions, shape rules, and compromise. They shift responsibilities and experiment with new ways of solving problems.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: In McCubbins' family typology, a family that is LOW in family coherence and LOW in family hardiness is classified as:
options: Regenerative
Durable
Secure
Vulnerable
Rhythmic

rationale.text: Using the Family Hardiness-Coherence grid: LOW coherence + LOW hardiness = VULNERABLE. Vulnerable families are more complacent, less likely to try new things, tend to repeat the same behaviors, and are less likely to encourage each other to be active or learn new things.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: DURABLE families are characterized by:
options: High hardiness and high coherence
High coherence and low hardiness
Low hardiness but strong coping repertoire characterized by caring and trust
High flexibility and high bonding
High routines and high valuing of routines

rationale.text: DURABLE families have LESSER basic internal strength (low hardiness) but compensate with a STRONG COPING REPERTOIRE characterized by caring, respect, trust, reduced tension, and calmness. They may seem weak internally but cope well through strong relational skills.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The CIRCUMPLEX MODEL identifies THREE key concepts for understanding family functioning. These are:
options: Hardiness, Coherence, and Resilience
Cohesion, Flexibility, and Communication
Adaptability, Partnership, and Growth
Bonding, Routines, and Flexibility
Enmeshment, Disengagement, and Triangulation

rationale.text: The Circumplex Model (Olson) has THREE key concepts: (1) COHESION — emotional bonding between family members; (2) FLEXIBILITY — quality and expression of leadership, organization, role relationships, and rule negotiation; (3) COMMUNICATION — positive communication skills utilized by the family system.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The main hypothesis of the Circumplex Model is:
options: Extremely high cohesion always leads to healthy family functioning
Balanced levels of cohesion and flexibility are most conducive to healthy family functioning
Low cohesion is always associated with better outcomes
High flexibility always leads to dysfunction
Communication is more important than cohesion and flexibility combined

rationale.text: The Circumplex Model's main hypothesis: BALANCED levels of cohesion and flexibility (neither too low nor too high) are MOST conducive to healthy family functioning. Unbalanced levels (very low or very high) are associated with PROBLEMATIC family functioning.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Von and his wife let their 14-year-old daughter's preferences take priority over their ideals, not wanting to force her to conform to their standards. What type of parenting style do they demonstrate?
options: Authoritarian
Democratic
Permissive
Rejecting
Uninvolved

rationale.text: PERMISSIVE parenting: parents let the child's preferences take priority over their ideals and rarely force the child to conform to their standards. The children are in control rather than the parents. Located in the upper right quadrant (high chaos and enmeshment) of the Circumplex Model. Children exhibit impulsive-aggressive behavior.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: Children of DEMOCRATIC (authoritative) parents exhibit which behavior pattern?
options: Conflicted and irritable, unhappy and unstable
Impulsive and rebellious, low achieving
Energetic-friendly, self-reliant and cheerful, achievement oriented
Immature, psychologically troubled
Lonely and withdrawn, low achieving

rationale.text: Children of DEMOCRATIC parents (Baumrind, 1995) exhibit ENERGETIC-FRIENDLY behavior: very self-reliant, cheerful, cope well with stress, and are achievement oriented. Democratic parents establish clear rules and expectations, discuss them with the child, and use both reason and power to enforce their standards.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: AUTHORITARIAN parenting is located in which quadrant of the Circumplex Model?
options: Upper left — high chaos and disengagement
Upper right — high chaos and enmeshment
Lower right — high rigidity and enmeshment
Lower left — high rigidity and disengagement
Center — balanced cohesion and flexibility

rationale.text: AUTHORITARIAN parenting = lower right quadrant = high RIGIDITY + high ENMESHMENT. These parents have rigid rules and expect/demand obedience and loyalty. As the style becomes more intense, the family moves toward 'rigidly enmeshed.' Children tend to be conflicted-irritable, moody, unhappy, and unfriendly.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: The UNINVOLVED parenting style is located in which quadrant of the Circumplex Model?
options: Upper left — high chaos and disengagement
Upper right — high chaos and enmeshment
Lower right — high rigidity and enmeshment
Lower left — high rigidity and disengagement
Center

rationale.text: UNINVOLVED parenting = upper left quadrant = high CHAOS + DISENGAGEMENT. Parents often ignore the child, letting preferences prevail as long as they don't interfere with the parents' activities. As it becomes more extreme, it moves toward 'chaotic disengaged.' Children are often withdrawn loners and low achievers.

subject: Family & Community Health
question: In the VERSATILE FAMILY typology matrix, PLIANT families are characterized by:
options: High flexibility but low bonding — emotionally disconnected but able to handle stress flexibly
Low flexibility and low bonding — unable to deal with stress
